title: Barclays Tweaks S&P 500 Target for Rest of 2026 - Yahoo Finance
text: Barclays Tweaks S&P 500 Target for Rest of 2026 Moz Farooque ACCA September 10, 2026 2 min read BCS ^GSPC This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Barclays has raised its year-end 2026 S&P 500 target to 7,950 from 7,800 after a standout technology earnings season strengthened confidence in AI-driven profit growth. The revised target sits about 3.6% above Tuesday's 7,673.52 close. That leaves upside, but hardly an unrestricted bull call. Barclays is raising its earnings expectations much more aggressively than the index target because higher rates limit how much valuations can expand. Is SPY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Head of U.S. equity strategy Venu Krishna highlighted technology execution and improving visibility into profits supported by AI investment. Barclays increased its 2026 S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecast to $365 from $337, an 8.3% upgrade. Earnings, Not Valuations, Drive Barclays' Call The distinction matters for investors. If the S&P 500 reaches 7,950 on $365 of earnings, it would trade at roughly 21.8 times the firm's forecast. Barclays appears willing to recognize stronger corporate profits without assuming investors will pay dramatically richer multiples for them. Continued AI capital spending and resilient economic activity underpin the outlook. Technology companies have converted heavy infrastructure investment into stronger revenue and earnings visibility, reinforcing the idea that artificial intelligence remains a profit catalyst rather than merely a valuation story. Risks remain substantial. Barclays cited uncertainty surrounding the durability of AI spending, sticky inflation, geopolitical tension and limited room for multiple expansion. A more hawkish interest-rate outlook could pressure valuations even if earnings estimates continue rising. The S&P 500 is already up nearly 12% in 2026, making further gains increasingly dependent on companies delivering rather than investors becoming more optimistic. Barclays kept its year-end 2027 target at 8,800. Its upgrade also follows HSBC's move to 8,100 from 7,650 for 2026. Together, the calls show Wall Street leaning toward continued gains powered by earnings, with less confidence in a broad valuation rerating. For investors, that makes technology execution, AI returns and profit revisions the critical market signals ahead. Terms and Privacy Policy Privacy Dashboard More Info
